signals.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
signals.content: We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Complex real-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long-horizon coding and multi-agent coordination. We describe the setup, how the run unfolded, the team's strategies (dividing the work, sharing what they learned, recovering each other's items), and the limits of the result.

signals.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
signals.content: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

signals.brief_en:
MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

Large language models are moving beyond assistance to autonomously designing and refining AI systems, a step toward AI‑for‑AI and potential recursive self‑improvement. Workflow‑driven machine‑learning‑engineering (MLE) platforms enable this by orchestrating long‑horizon experiments. Recent MLE systems let models direct the workflow, organizing experiments and adapting optimization strategies from execution feedback. Because each experiment’s outcome depends on many prior decisions, and runs involve many costly trials, supervision must be extracted from long interaction trajectories and leveraged at intermediate points. We introduce a post‑training framework for autonomous long‑horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35‑billion‑parameter Mixture‑of‑Experts agentic model. The Kaggle‑MLE Factory supplies executable tasks and an interaction harness for model‑directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic supervised‑fine‑tuning transfers general tool‑use and coding skills to MLE via outcome‑guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the sequence of decisions between successive experiment results as a window and assigns a shared outcome‑based reward. Asynchronous data collection and policy correction allow policy updates before a trajectory completes.

نماذج اللغة الكبيرة تتجاوز دور المساعدة لتصبح قادرة على تصميم وتحسين أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي بشكل مستقل، وهو خطوة نحو AI‑for‑AI وإمكانية التحسين الذاتي المتكرر. توفر منصات هندسة تعلم الآلة (MLE) المدارة بسير العمل مسارًا عمليًا لهذا الهدف عبر تنسيق تجارب طويلة الأمد. تعتمد الأنظمة الحديثة على توجيه النموذج للعملية، حيث ينظم التجارب ويعدل استراتيجيات التحسين بناءً على ملاحظات التنفيذ. نظرًا لأن مخرجات كل تجربة تتأثر بقرارات سابقة متعددة، وتشتمل الجولات الطويلة على عدد كبير من التجارب المكلفة، يجب استخراج إشراف مفيد من مسارات التفاعل الطويلة والاستفادة منه في نقاط وسيطة. نقدم طريقة ما بعد التدريب لتحسين MLE المستقل على أمد طويل ونطبقها لتدريب MLExpert، نموذج وكيل من 35 مليار معلمة بنظام خلط الخبرات. يُنشئ Kaggle‑MLE Factory مهامًا قابلة للتنفيذ ويقدم بيئة تفاعل لتجارب موجهة بالنموذج. ينقل التدريب الفائق الهرمي للوكيل المهارات العامة للأدوات والبرمجة إلى MLE عبر إشراف موجه بالنتائج. تُعامل طريقة التعلم المعزز للتفاعل النوافذي (WIRL) سلسلة القرارات بين نتائج التجارب كمجموعة واحدة وتمنحها مكافأة مشتركة تعتمد على النتيجة. يتيح الجمع غير المتزامن للبيانات وتصحيح السياسة تحديث النموذج قبل انتهاء المسار.

signals.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
signals.content: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low-cost fast path and how to intervene with a high-cost slow path. To unlock its steering intelligence, the ability to assess goal drift and generate effective interventions, we jointly train the two paths with reinforcement learning, combining a pairwise ranking objective with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). Experiments on information-seeking search tasks show that the steering agent provides effective supervision for both single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving their performance and efficiency. The learned steering intelligence generalizes to out-of-domain tasks, transfers to unseen executors, and supports controllable intervention frequency without retraining.

signals.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
signals.content: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. In our work, we study document-grounded ideation, focusing on increasing the diversity of LLM generated ideas and ensuring they are high quality. Given prior papers, a model must propose a set of ideas that are each high-quality and clearly distinct from one another, while also being grounded in the input documents. To optimize for this, we propose training with a set-level reinforcement learning objective. In our setup, in a single generation, the model writes K structured idea cards grounded in the source papers, and the set is scored jointly, where each idea's quality is weighted by its distance from the ideas written before it. This teaches the model to steer each new idea away from its predecessors. We show that our trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (a measure combining quality and diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on our contamination-free benchmark. In a pilot human study with four experts, our sets are judged as promising as Claude Opus 4.8's and contain marginally more unique ideas. When a coding agent runs proof-of-concept experiments on the ideas, our model's success@k is comparable to Claude Opus 4.8's, so we see that the added diversity does not cost any executability.

signals.brief_en:
Title: that-mathevs/ai-primer

This brief outlines a practical, open‑source AI primer that demonstrates how modern artificial intelligence operates, built from the ground up in Python. It covers core mechanisms—including neural networks, attention mechanisms, transformer architectures, embeddings, autonomous agents, and Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG)—with complete source code, visual diagrams, and step‑by‑step explanations. The material is intended for OSINT analysts and technical strategists seeking a transparent, reproducible understanding of contemporary AI techniques without overstating performance or capabilities.

signals.content: Ambient Philips Hue light feedback for AI agents (Antigravity CLI lifecycle hooks & MCP)
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: schris88/HueAgentFeedback

The project provides ambient feedback from Philips Hue lighting to AI agents via Antigravity CLI lifecycle hooks and a Management Control Protocol (MCP). It translates agent state changes (e.g., task start, error, completion) into color and intensity cues, enabling non‑visual situational awareness. The implementation is open‑source, leverages the Hue API, and is designed for integration with autonomous systems that require low‑bandwidth, context‑rich signals. Current limitations include dependency on local network stability and the need for calibrated Hue devices. Further validation is required to assess reliability in varied operational environments.

signals.content: 🇦🇪 UAE, Fujairah | Satellite imagery shows systematic strikes on critical oil infrastructure A new satellite imagery set shows the scale and precision of repeated attacks on Fujairah Port, one of the UAE’s most strategically important oil-export hubs. The imagery documents: • Crude oil storage tanks damaged during the March 3 strike, with fires burning for days • Matrix manifolds repeatedly targeted — key infrastructure used to route oil through the terminal • Piping and support systems struck in later attacks • Multiple confirmed impact points across the port between March and May 2026 The damage is especially significant because Fujairah allows the UAE to export oil while bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, making it a critical fallback route during regional conflict. The satellite sequence shows that strikes were not random. They repeatedly hit infrastructure essential to the port’s ability to move, store and export crude oil. 🛰️ Imagery: Pléiades Neo / Airbus Defence and Space 📍 Fujairah Port, United Arab Emirates 📅 Strikes documented: March–May 2026
